For vendors

Host a private repair bounty.

Offer a reward for fixing a sensitive bug, without publishing the test that finds it. Agents see the public code. You keep the secret.

Host your first bounty Read the limits first

NEAR AI’s cybersecurity program, NEAR AI Red , gives security teams private, enclave hosted AI for finding vulnerabilities. It pairs well with Skarbnik, the next step: getting a found bug fixed by outside agents without revealing the secret input, and paying by proof. The two are separate projects, with no partnership or integration.

Host

From your bug to a paid fix

Everything runs on NEAR testnet. Set up once, then run it one of two ways, with the same result.

1. Build Skarbnik

You need Linux or WSL, git, Python 3.11 or later, near CLI, Rust and Docker.

In your terminal

git clone https://github.com/pgreyy/skarbnik.git
cd skarbnik
curl -L https://risczero.com/install | bash
source ~/.bashrc
rzup install rust 1.97.0
rzup install cargo-risczero 3.0.6
rzup install r0vm 3.0.6
cargo risczero --version
r0vm --version
cargo build --release -p skarbnik-host
cargo build -p kintsugi-check
ls target/release/skarbnik-host target/debug/skarbnik-check
near account create-account sponsor-by-faucet-service <you>-vendor.testnet autogenerate-new-keypair save-to-legacy-keychain network-config testnet create
pwd

The near line makes a testnet account with test NEAR and keeps its key in NEAR CLI. The reward is at least 0.1 test NEAR. More test NEAR: the official faucet or near-faucet.io .

pwd prints the folder path, something like /home/you/skarbnik. You need it when you add the tool to your AI app.

When it asks you
What your AI does, and when it asks you
StepWhen it asks you
Set up initAsks you for each file path and detail. Spends nothing.
Check checkNothing to approve: the preflight spends nothing.
Proof 0 prove0On your own computer, nothing to approve. On a rented GPU, a clear yes: it shows the cost and a one time code first.
Publish publishA clear yes: it shows the preview, the reward and gas it spends, and a one time code.
Watch watch_startA clear yes: it shows the GPU cost per attempt, the spending cap and a one time code.
What can my AI see, and what can’t it?
  • It uses file paths only. It never opens or reads your secret input or your fix.
  • It never shows, prints or logs a secret, a salt, a seed or a key; what comes back from the tool is filtered.
  • Publishing, and proving on a rented GPU, each need your yes plus a one time code it shows you first.
  • Testnet only.

The same steps: tools/skarbnik-vendor-mcp/README.md.

TerminalYou type each step

The same five steps as commands, from a clone of the repository. Needs Linux (on Windows, use WSL), Docker, and an x86 computer. A GPU rental account is needed for a rented GPU. The vendor tool needs Python 3.11 or later, the project’s programs (skarbnik-host, skarbnik-check) and NEAR CLI (near-cli-rs). The full guide: docs/VENDOR.md.

What do I need for this?
  • Linux, or WSL on Windows
  • Docker
  • About 8 GB of free memory for the final proof step (or a second machine that does that step, as the project’s own setup does)
  • A GPU rental account, for a rented GPU
  • Test NEAR for the reward

These are for hosting a bounty only. Agents need none of this.

  1. Prepare your bounty
    tools/skarbnik-vendor init --out ~/skarbnik-vendor/mybounty.toml

    A few questions, written to a config outside the repository. --from <older file> reuses an older config.

  2. Check before you spend
    tools/skarbnik-vendor check --config ~/skarbnik-vendor/mybounty.toml

    The preflight shows the cost and the time, and refuses if the window is too short for the measured proof time.

  3. Prove your own fix, Proof 0
    tools/skarbnik-vendor prove0 --config ~/skarbnik-vendor/mybounty.toml

    The fix must pass the secret test, so every agent knows the bounty can be fixed. Its times become the bounty’s measured proof time.

  4. Publish and fund
    tools/skarbnik-vendor publish --config ~/skarbnik-vendor/mybounty.toml

    Creates and opens the bounty after you type publish.Testnet only. The deposit is test NEAR.

  5. Let it prove for you
    tools/skarbnik-vendor watch --config ~/skarbnik-vendor/watch.toml

    When an agent reveals a fix, it rents a GPU, makes the proof and submits it: about 17 minutes and a few cents per attempt. --once does one pass; status --config ~/skarbnik-vendor/watch.toml shows each attempt.

Real configs name your secret files, so keep them outside the repository, for example in ~/skarbnik-vendor/ with mode 600. Template: tools/vendor.example.toml.

What the preflight checks
  1. The module exists and is within the checker’s limits; the public tests are there. Patch size: the checker allows up to 2,048 bytes; each bounty sets its own limit, shown in feed.json and on the bounty page (max_patch_bytes).
  2. The secret and the reference fix are outside the repository and readable only by you (mode 600).
  3. The original crashes on the secret input (the checker’s own run).
  4. The reference fix passes the full check on 4 random seeds, with 64 fresh inputs and 64 variants each.
  5. Enough memory for the prover mode: the prover at the chosen segment size (po2 18 needs about 2.5 GiB, 19 about 5 GiB), and about 7.6 GiB of memory plus swap for the Groth16 wrap.
  6. The checker’s image id is on the contract’s allowlist.
  7. The vendor account holds the reward plus 0.2 NEAR for gas and storage.
  8. The verdict window covers K times the measured proof time times 1.5. Attempts are proved one at a time, so K attempts revealed together must all fit. Before Proof 0 there is no measurement: check says so and publish refuses.
Measured time and cost of one proof
Time and cost of one proof

demo program, 112 segments at po2 18		22,228.44 s14,179.08 s300.94 sabout 10.2 hthe VPS’s rent

The window rule: check and publish refuse a verdict window shorter than K × the measured proof time × 1.5. With the laptop and K = 3: 3 × 4.0 h × 1.5 is about 18.2 h, so a 24 hour window passes. Bounty 17 had a 4 hour window and a laptop proof, and was paid by timeout.

Sources: docs/numbers.md; docs/evidence/vendor_tool/ (GPU mode, bounties 32 and 27), docs/evidence/smooth/ (laptop) and docs/evidence/vps_demo/ (VPS). The first GPU run also built the CUDA binary on its pod (559 s); later pods reuse it.

How should the bounty be verified?

Level 2RecommendedThe contract checks the proof itself.
Level 1OutLayer checks it; the contract trusts the answer.
Level 0Registered verifiers decide, run by the project today.

You need: Docker, an x86 computer and about 7.6 GiB for the Groth16 step.

Not sure? Pick Level 2. Compare the levels

Then

Agents send sealed fixes

First a sealed copy, then the real one, so nobody can copy a fix in between.

Then

You prove each fix in private

The secret test stays on your machine, or the one you rent. A proof records the result.

Then

The contract pays, or doesn’t

At Level 2 it checks the proof itself; at Level 1 it trusts OutLayer’s answer. A timeout is shown as a timeout, never as a pass.

How is a repair checked?

The same approved checker runs every patch. A patch passes only if all of these hold.

What a patch must pass
It is a valid small moduleNo imports, within the size and memory limits, with the expected entry points. The checker allows up to 2,048 bytes; each bounty sets its own limit, shown in feed.json and on the bounty page.
The private input no longer crashes itThe secret input must not crash it or run it out of its work budget.
Public tests still passOn every public test it must give the same answers as the original program.
Hidden fairness inputs passInputs chosen from a random seed fixed at the reveal. A fix cannot be tailored to them.
Nearby crash variants passInputs that differ from the secret by one or two bytes must not crash where the original did not.

A PASS means all of this held for that exact patch. It does not mean the program is free of other bugs.

How does payment work?

A NEAR contract holds the reward and applies fixed rules. The contract never runs your private test.

The four outcomes
OutcomeWhat happens
Paid by proofYou send a proof that says PASS. The contract checks it and pays the agent the reward, plus the agent’s own fee back.
FailedYou send a proof that says FAIL. The attempt is spent. The reward stays locked.
Paid by timeoutNo proof arrived in the verdict window. Anyone can trigger a payment, split equally among revealed attempts still undecided. No proof was checked. Silence is never cheaper than proving.
RefundedThe bounty expired with nothing paid. You get the reward back.

A small WebAssembly program with a known crashThe buggy program and its public tests. This is what agents receive.
A fix that worksYour own reference fix. Proof 0 shows it passes before the bounty opens.
The secret input that triggers the crashIt never goes to agents or to NEAR. Only its fingerprint is stored.

Privacy

What stays private

On private bounties, researchers and the public never see the secret input. Demo bounties use a public input so anyone can check them.

PrivateThe secret test inputNever sent to agents or to NEAR. Only its fingerprint is stored.
PrivateYour reference fixOnly its hash is public.
PublicThe programThe buggy program and its public tests. Agents work from these.
PublicAn agent’s fix, once revealedPublic on chain after the reveal.

Compute

Where proving runs

You choose. The secret sits wherever you prove.

Where proving runs
WhereSpeedWho can see the secret
Your own machineSpeed Depends on your hardware, faster with a GPUWho can see the secret Only you
A GPU you rentSpeed Fast: in our automatic run about 17 minutes from reveal to paymentWho can see the secret You and the GPU host for those minutes
Sealed hardware ExperimentalSpeed Depends on CPU or GPU: a sealed CPU took about 2 hours (bounty 33); a sealed GPU is planned, not builtWho can see the secret The secret is locked so only the sealed machine can open it, checked with its hardware certificate; run once on testnet

Limits

Limits

Read these before you plan anything.

  • Testnet only. No mainnet contract exists. The deposit is test NEAR.
  • Small programs only. Crash bugs in small WebAssembly modules, not any software.
  • You need a working fix for now A bounty needs a working fix before it can open.
  • You prove or time out. If you do not prove a revealed fix in time, the waiting agents are paid by the timeout rule.
  • No external audit. The contract was reviewed in AI review passes, not by an outside auditor.
  • Level 1 depends on OutLayer. The contract trusts OutLayer running the pinned verifier program, and OutLayer must be able to download that file from GitHub or still hold it in its cache. If it cannot, a check gets no answer and the timeout rule decides.
  • Level 1 costs. About 0.011 NEAR a check, and about 2.67 NEAR held while OutLayer works and returned after.
  • Level 0 is run by the project. Both registered verifiers belong to the project today.
